newsitem.title: USA: Sherwin-Williams to acquire Thompson Minwax.
newsitem.headline: Sherwin-Williams to acquire Thompson Minwax.

text.p: Sherwin-Williams Co. said Friday it has a definitive agreement to acquire Thompson Minwax Holding Corp. from affiliates of private investment firm Forstmann Little & Co. for $830 million in cash.
New York-based Forstmann had acquired Thompson Minwax brands, a line of stains and varnishes, from Eastman Kodak Co. in 1994 for $700 million.

With annual sales of about $375 million, Thompson Minwax makes Minwax brand interior stains and varnishes, Thompson's exterior water sealers and stains, and Formby's and Red Devil finishing and enamel coating products.
The company, based in Upper Saddle River, N.J., also owns Roncraft, maker of Ronseal interior and exterior stains in Britain.
Cleveland-based Sherwin-Williams, founded in 1866, is a leading manufacturer, distributor and marketer of coatings and related products in the United States and Latin America.

"Thompson Minwax's well known brands added to our existing Dutch Boy, Pratt & Lambert, Martin-Senour and Krylon brands will provide our customers with a broader product assortment and complement the distribution of our current branded coatings products," said John G. Breen, chairman and chief executive of Sherwin-Williams.

"Roncraft will provide us a well recognised brand and access to important distribution channels in the U.K. markets. The broader assortment of products the Thompson Minwax acquisition brings to our company will help extend our 18 years of consecutive earnings improvement into the future."
The deal is expected to close in late 1996.
Founded in 1978, Forstmann Little is a private investment firm that has invested over $13 billion in 21 acquisitions, including General Instrument, Ziff-Davis Publishing and Gulfstream Aerospace.
Sherwin-Williams' stock fell 12.5 cents to $56.625 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
